wa_mount_shuksan_white_salmon_glacier.approach: From the small pull-off at the old White Salmon Lodge on the Mount Baker Highway, walk around the gate and follow the old road past the lodge site for about a mile to where it ends at an old clearcut. With good snow cover, descend northeast to White Salmon Creek and follow the valley up to the toe of the White Salmon Glacier. Without it, hold your height through the clearcut and contour, losing elevation only to get around rock bands and stream crossings, to stay out of the slide alder in the valley bottom. Bivy sites sit among the rock outcrops along the eastern edge of the glacier.
wa_mount_shuksan_white_salmon_glacier.why: Matches variant 0 (White Salmon Lodge road, primary). The old paragraph (Lake Ann Trail over Austin Pass to a ~6,500 ft moraine camp) is the Fisher Chimneys approach, not the White Salmon Glacier. Mountain Project route 107476711 (https://www.mountainproject.com/route/107476711/white-salmon-glacier): start at the White Salmon Lodge pull-off on the Mt Baker Hwy, gate, road to old clearcut; good snow = descend NE to White Salmon Creek to glacier toe; poor snow = contour; 'good bivy sites at rock outcroppings along eastern edge of White Salmon'. Corroborated by engineeredforadventure.com (Mar 2020) and turns-all-year May 2 TR. 'About a mile' is carried over from variant 0's existing notes, not newly introduced. NOT EDITED but also wrong for this route: approach_logistics.trailhead = 'Lake Ann Trailhead (Austin Pass)' with Austin Pass coords (48.8502,-121.6861); should be the White Salmon Lodge pull-off on SR 542 (coords not verified here, so not proposed).

wa_inner_constance_standard.why: Not misfiled. The Lake Constance - South Gully - East Ridge line (Olympic guide Route 2A) is an INNER Constance route: https://trailcatjim.com/mt-constance-inner-peak/ ('Mt Constance: Inner Peak via Lake Constance-South Gully-East Ridge') reaches 'a broad couloir that begins just north of The Thumb', takes a steeper secondary couloir into a snow-filled defile with 5-10 ft moats on each side, stems between snow and rock, was hit by a 'refrigerator-size block of snow', then a snow couloir to the east ridge crest and Class 2-3 pillow basalt to the summit. Every element of variant 0's notes/hazards/baseFinding matches. The Thumb is an Avalanche Canyon landmark on the canyon's WEST side (Inner Constance's side); the Mount Constance route from the same couloir is the South Chute, which climbs EAST - and variant 0 already says exactly that ('the South Chute (which belongs to MOUNT Constance) and the South Gully (which belongs to INNER Constance)'). Inner Constance forms the other (west) side of Avalanche Canyon (Wikipedia 'Inner Constance'). No change proposed.

wa_mount_daniel_lynch_glacier.why: Not misfiled. From Peggy's Pond the route traverses around the 6,300 ft contour below the Daniel Glacier to Lynch draw and walks ACROSS frozen Pea Soup Lake onto the ice above the low rocks; late season 'Lynch Draw may be flooded and Pea Soup Lake melted out' (Mountaineers route page Mount Daniel/Lynch Glacier, https://www.mountaineers.org/activities/routes-places/mount-daniel-lynch-glacier, and its trip reports; wenatcheeoutdoors.org/2016/07/20/daniel-mt/). Variant 0's own baseFinding describes this same lake crossing, so frozen-lake/moat season text belongs to variant 0. Variant 1 (Dip Top Gap) descends to the lake's OUTLET on the west end (trailcatjim Dip Top loop, late July; Mountain Project 124973025) and does not cross the lake, so its season text correctly keys only on the moat. Cosmetic only (not proposed, since the problem as stated is not real): variant 0 season lacks a leading month window and its phrase 'The Pea Soup approach' is ambiguous; if a wording pass is wanted, e.g. 'Jun-mid Jul, while Pea Soup Lake is frozen and the moat closed; the lake crossing gets hard once it melts' (no new facts).
